set.st: For the Fourth of July 1871 the Menasha Turners held their entertainment 'on the old picnic grounds on the Island' (Doty Island), after a procession from Turner Hall at 9 a.m. The grounds were already 'old' by then. Old picnic grounds are where coins and small things were lost.
src: 'Fourth of July Festivities / Turners', Menasha Saturday Evening Press, 1 Jul 1871, p. 3 (Newspapers.com 445296630) (Neb's clipping)

tw-mn-henderson-ritter-beer-casks.st: In May 1926 a digging party at 'the ruins of the old Ritter brewery' was halted by heavy masonry, and old-timers doubted the casks were there.
tw-mn-henderson-ritter-beer-casks.t: In 1926 the site was called the old Ritter brewery ruins; whether it is the 'Jno. Enes Brewery' of the 1894 Sanborn is unconfirmed (Enes may have been Ritter's successor).
src: 'Beer Treasure Hunt Is Halted by Heavy Barriers of Masonry', Star Tribune (Minneapolis), 23 May 1926, p. 10 (Newspapers.com 181857287)
